modern: In the constitution of the rational being I see no virtue which is opposed to justice; but I see a virtue which is opposed to love of pleasure, and that is self-control.
original: In the constitution of the rational animal I see no virtue which is opposed to justice; but I see a virtue which is opposed to love of pleasure, and that is temperance.
notification: In the constitution of the rational being I see no virtue which is opposed to justice; but I see a virtue which is opposed to love of pleasure, and that is self-control.
notification_original: In the constitution of the rational animal I see no virtue which is opposed to justice; but I see a virtue which is opposed to love of pleasure, and that is temperance.

explained.summary: When Marcus examines what a reasoning being is made for, he finds no virtue that works against fairness to others. But he does find one that works against the love of pleasure: self-control. Justice is central to our nature; pleasure-seeking is what needs reining in.
